record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How should adversarial training and robust optimization be adapted to federated learning when samples may be seen only a few times, data are non-IID, perturbation bounds cannot be chosen by inspecting data centrally, and adversarial-example generation may exceed on-device memory or power budgets?

evidence.quote: Adapting adversarial training methods to federated learning

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a global model is trained across a large, heterogeneous population of client devices. Each client holds a local dataset, and the local distributions are non-identically and non-independently distributed (non-IID) across clients. Training proceeds by repeated rounds in which a server distributes the current model to a subset of clients, each client performs local updates on its data, and the server aggregates the resulting updates. The setting has the following constraints:

(a) Any given training sample on a client may be visited only a small number of times during the entire training process.
(b) Raw client data cannot be inspected centrally, so global statistics needed to set hyperparameters (in particular, the magnitude of allowable adversarial perturbations) are not directly available.
(c) Each client device has bounded memory, compute, and power, which may be insufficient to run standard procedures for generating adversarial examples (e.g., multi-step projected gradient ascent inner loops) at training time.

Design a training procedure that performs adversarial training or, more generally, robust optimization in this federated setting, and provide formal guarantees on the adversarial robustness of the resulting global model. Specifically:

1. Define a notion of robust risk appropriate to the federated, non-IID setting, including how the per-client perturbation set should be chosen given that data cannot be examined centrally.
2. Specify an algorithm that produces adversarial perturbations and model updates under the per-sample visit limit and the on-device memory/compute constraints, and prove convergence of the algorithm to a stationary point of the chosen robust objective.
3. Establish bounds on the robust generalization error of the trained model in terms of the data heterogeneity, the number of times each sample is used, and the resources available on each client.

Either provide such a procedure with the stated guarantees, or prove obstructions showing that no algorithm satisfying the constraints can achieve nontrivial certified robustness in this regime.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2023–2025) on robust and adversarial federated learning explicitly list adapting adversarial training to federated settings under non-IID data, limited sample reuse, and tight on-device resource budgets as an ongoing research direction. Several partial methods (e.g., federated adversarial training variants, clustering-based defenses, dual adversarial schemes) exist, but no method addresses all the listed constraints simultaneously with formal robust-generalization guarantees, and recent systematic reviews continue to flag it as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: A Systematic Literature Review of Robust Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys robust FL issues and lists adversarial training under heterogeneity and resource constraints among future research directions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of adapting adversarial training to FL under non-IID, resource-constrained settings remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Delving into the Adversarial Robustness of Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Test accuracy reduces for plainly trained and adversarially trained models under non-IID data; adversarial training can hurt performance.
status_evidence.claim: Standard adversarial training degrades under non-IID FL, indicating the question is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Federated Learning: Attacks, Defenses, Opportunities, and Challenges
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses on-device constraints and adversarial threats in FL as open challenges.
status_evidence.claim: Adversarial training adaptation under device and data constraints is still listed as an open challenge.
